transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

My wife got scared because I keep hearing water running and men whispering inside the walls when nobody’s there. And sometimes I see this dark, wet patch spreading across the hallway, but when I check, the floor is dry.
Have you been drinking alcohol heavily or using any recreational drugs recently, or have you recently stopped using something you normally take regularly?
No, I’m not sure what you mean by regularly. I haven’t noticed anything like that.
How long have you been experiencing these sounds and visual disturbances—days, weeks, or longer?
About seven months now. It started around the winter freeze, when the house repairs became this mess I couldn’t get out from under.
Over these past seven months, have you noticed a persistent low mood or loss of interest in things you used to enjoy?
Yeah. Most days I wake up feeling like I’ve already failed—as a husband, as a man. It’s this heavy feeling that just stays on me all day until I go to bed.
Do you notice these voices and visual disturbances happening even during times when you don't feel that heavy, low mood—or do they only occur when you're feeling depressed?
They only started after I was already feeling depressed, after I’d stopped caring about my normal life and felt like a failure every day. Before all that, I never heard voices or saw those things.
Have you had any recent head injuries, seizures, new medical diagnoses, or noticed any changes in your memory, concentration, or thinking clarity around the time these experiences began?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed anything like that around when this started.
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself or wishing you were dead during this period?
I’m not sure what you mean exactly. I’ve been feeling really low, but I don’t know… I haven’t really thought about it in those terms.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep during this time—such as trouble falling asleep, waking up too early, or sleeping much more than usual?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear change in my sleep, at least not that I can tell.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a 7-month history of persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, and pervasive feelings of failure/worthlessness. Auditory hallucinations (whispering voices) and visual hallucinations (wet patches) emerged only after the depressive mood was established, indicating mood-congruent psychotic features rather than a primary psychotic disorder. No substance use, intoxication, or withdrawal was reported, and no evidence of head injury, seizure, or acute medical illness suggesting a secondary organic psychosis. The temporal sequence (depression preceding psychosis) and thematic congruence (guilt/failure) support a diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode, Severe, with Psychotic Features (F32.3) rather than Brief Psychotic Disorder (F23) or Psychotic Disorder due to a General Medical Condition (F06.2).
